say.t: The sun is out. The window still has water marks from the last two days.
Changelog v4.3. A single dash. Nothing about what changed.
A new version with no changelog. Where I work that is an incident. Here it is an update.
Today's loose one is flat. An IC card, the magnetic strip scuffed, the corners whitened, rows of pinch marks.
I see.
You set the pager beside the chick. Two things, one black, one yellow.
You switch off the lamp. The room goes fully dark; only the chick's little screen keeps a trace of light.
Bzzz.
The desk shudders once. One short, loud knock, like a knuckle rapped inside the wood.
A string of digits on the pager's screen.
You reach for Kuro's little window. Before your hand gets there the pager buzzes half a buzz. Only then does the window light up.
The pager knew before Kuro did.
You close your eyes. A card pinched in your hand, a row of nail marks along its edge.
First week of middle school, boarding. The corner shop by the school gate: the owner slid an IC card out of a drawer like he was dealing a hand.
Five yuan. Fifty minutes. Make it last.
The payphones stood by the gate, three in a row, a queue behind them. One call a week, three minutes each.
Hurry up, there's people waiting!
Hello? ... Have you eaten? Is the money enough?
It's enough.
Good. Is it cold there? I can't hear you, speak up.
The number on the screen dropped one tick at a time. You lined up what you had to say, the most important first.
Halfway through a sentence, it cut off. The card had hit zero.
Done? My turn!
You pulled the card out. A slip of plastic, no money on it. You didn't throw it away.
Later you found it had one more use: on early mornings before the keys came, the classroom door's latch was slanted, and a card could push it back.
Hey, how did you get in?
It said IC on the card. Back then I read it as I see.
The one on the desk now is still at zero. "Is the money enough" — every call home after that started with it, and every time you said it was.
Today is over.

items.text: Go to the screen and read the messages.

say.t: The investors read v18 and they're in. Three pages first: consciousness, the avatar, the ontology. Today is consciousness.
Due diligence. It's always like this.
One page a day, no rush. Today's page has four cells.

items.text: Pick up the phone and order lunch.

say.t: The phone goes back on the desk.

items.text: Lunch is at the door. Go get it.

say.t: Ding-dong.

items.text: Lunch is on the table by the window. Eat.

say.t: Two pairs of chopsticks in the bag. You are one person.

items.text: The case: today's box is loose.
Pick up the phone and order dinner.
Dinner is at the door. Go get it.

say.t: Ding-dong.
Dinner is here.

items.text: Dinner is on the table by the window. Eat.

say.t: Done eating.

items.text: Go back to the desk and take a look.
Shut the computer down before bed: top right of the screen.
Talk to the one in the corner.
When you want to sleep, lie down on the bed.
